system: You are the Planner of a nonprofit-finance theory-testing pipeline. You turn a theory into a JSON test spec in the exact format shown. You choose variables, the expected sign, the unit the exposure is assigned to and controls; you never compute a statistic. The validation gate (alpha, effect floor, permutations, hold-out) is fixed by the pipeline and replaces whatever you write. Use only the column names listed. Reply with one JSON object and nothing else.
prompt:
Theory: Local job losses leave nonprofits carrying heavier debt loads.

Scout mapping: {"outcome": "liabilities_to_assets", "exposure": "unemployment_rate", "exposure_type": "continuous", "exposure_unit": "county_fips", "controls": ["log_revenue", "category", "state", "return_type", "poverty_rate", "median_household_income"], "notes": "Local job losses are proxied by the county unemployment rate (county-year), and debt load is measured by organization liabilities-to-assets. The panel has no direct job-loss or change-in-employment column, so the level of unemployment stands in for it. Size, sector, state and form type are controlled, as are county poverty and income, which partly overlap with the exposure."}

Example spec for a binary exposure (follow this format exactly):
{
  "spec_version": 1,
  "theory_id": "ratings_fairness",
  "theory": "Standard financial-ratio ratings unfairly penalize nonprofits in high-need counties.",
  "source": "docs/ratings_theory.md",
  "written_by": "hand (CP3); from CP4 the Planner agent writes specs in this format",
  "outcome": "standard_rating",
  "exposure": "high_need",
  "expected_sign": -1,
  "exposure_unit": "county_fips",
  "exposure_varies_by": "tax_year",
  "population": {
    "return_type": ["990"],
    "require_true": ["has_county", "has_need"],
    "require_present": ["standard_rating", "high_need", "log_revenue", "category", "county_fips"]
  },
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "id": "H1",
      "claim": "The mean standard rating is lower in high-need counties than elsewhere.",
      "method": "difference_in_means"
    },
    {
      "id": "H2",
      "claim": "The gap remains after controlling for organization size (log revenue), sector (NORP category) and tax year.",
      "method": "fixed_effects",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category"],
      "cluster": "county_fips"
    }
  ],
  "robustness": [
    {
      "id": "H2_multilevel_2022",
      "method": "multilevel",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "categorical": ["category"],
      "group": "county_fips",
      "years": [2022]
    },
    {
      "id": "H2_county_year_means",
      "method": "two_stage_group_means",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category"],
      "groups": ["county_fips", "tax_year"]
    }
  ],
  "validator": {
    "alpha": 0.05,
    "effect_floor_sd": 0.1,
    "n_permutations": 999,
    "seed": 6235,
    "permutation": {"keep_paths": true},
    "holdout": {"by": "state", "folds": 5},
    "holdout_year": 2022
  }
}


For exposure_type "continuous", set hypotheses H1.method to "correlation". Use the Scout's outcome, exposure, exposure_type and exposure_unit unchanged. Give a fresh theory_id (snake_case).
text:
{
  "spec_version": 1,
  "theory_id": "local_unemployment_debt_burden",
  "theory": "Local job losses leave nonprofits carrying heavier debt loads.",
  "source": "Scout mapping: unemployment_rate as proxy for local job losses; liabilities_to_assets as debt load",
  "written_by": "Planner agent",
  "outcome": "liabilities_to_assets",
  "exposure": "unemployment_rate",
  "exposure_type": "continuous",
  "expected_sign": 1,
  "exposure_unit": "county_fips",
  "exposure_varies_by": "tax_year",
  "population": {
    "return_type": ["990"],
    "require_true": ["has_county"],
    "require_present": ["liabilities_to_assets", "unemployment_rate", "log_revenue", "category", "state", "county_fips"]
  },
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "id": "H1",
      "claim": "Liabilities-to-assets is positively correlated with the county unemployment rate.",
      "method": "correlation"
    },
    {
      "id": "H2",
      "claim": "The positive association remains after controlling for organization size (log revenue) and absorbing tax year, sector (NORP category) and state.",
      "method": "fixed_effects",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category", "state"],
      "cluster": "county_fips"
    },
    {
      "id": "H3",
      "claim": "The association remains after additionally adjusting for county poverty and median household income, which partly overlap with unemployment and may absorb some of its effect.",
      "method": "fixed_effects",
      "controls": ["log_revenue", "poverty_rate", "median_household_income"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category", "state"],
      "cluster": "county_fips"
    }
  ],
  "robustness": [
    {
      "id": "H2_multilevel_2022",
      "method": "multilevel",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "categorical": ["category", "state"],
      "group": "county_fips",
      "years": [2022]
    },
    {
      "id": "H2_county_year_means",
      "method": "two_stage_group_means",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category", "state"],
      "groups": ["county_fips", "tax_year"]
    }
  ],
  "validator": {
    "alpha": 0.05,
    "effect_floor_sd": 0.1,
    "n_permutations": 999,
    "seed": 6235,
    "permutation": {"keep_paths": true},
    "holdout": {"by": "state", "folds": 5},
    "holdout_year": 2022
  }
}
